title: Arithmetic nodal charts and their singular-point blowups
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $\pi$ generate its maximal ideal, let $k=R/(\pi)$, and let $n\geq1$. Put $M_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R[x,y]/(xy-\pi^n))$ and let $o$ be the closed point $(\pi,x,y)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $M_n$ is integral and normal (all its local rings are integrally closed domains), is flat over $R$, and has reduced nodal geometric curve fibres [def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. It is regular outside $o$, and is regular at $o$ exactly when $n=1$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Every local ring of $M_n$ has dimension at most $2$, and its local ring at $o$ has dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A smooth $R$-scheme of pure relative dimension one is regular and normal, and all its local rings have dimension at most $2$; at every closed point of its special fibre its local ring has dimension $2$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pure-dimension]. These normality, regularity and local-dimension assertions hold in any pointed etale local model: if pointed schemes have a common pointed etale neighbourhood over $\operatorname{Spec}R$, one with a map etale to the indicated model and the specified image point, then the other has the same asserted local properties [def-weil-etale-morphism].

For $n\geq2$, let $b:B_n=\operatorname{Bl}_oM_n\to M_n$ be the ordinary blowup of the reduced closed point [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its three affine charts, with their maps to $M_n$, are
$$R[x,t]/(xt-\pi),\quad y=x^{n-1}t^n;\qquad R[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2}),\quad x=\pi r,\ y=\pi s;\qquad R[y,t']/ (yt'-\pi),\quad x=y^{n-1}(t')^n.$$
The middle chart when $n=2$ means $rs=1$. Thus $B_n$ is flat with reduced nodal geometric curve fibres, and the only possibly nonregular point above $o$ is the origin in the middle chart when $n-2\geq2$; its local model is $M_{n-2}$. The geometric exceptional fibre is a smooth conic isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ if $n=2$, and two copies of $\mathbf P^1$ meeting in one point if $n>2$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. The map is an isomorphism off $o$. These chart and exceptional-fibre descriptions remain valid after etale pullback, with the blowup center the inverse image of $o$ and the exceptional fibre taken over a chosen point above $o$; they also apply to a blowup of the corresponding reduced point in a common pointed etale neighbourhood. No excellence, completeness, perfection, or restriction on the residue characteristic is assumed.

proof.text: The binomial normal-form theorem at $a=\pi^n$ makes $A_n$ a domain and all its local rings normal; its spectrum is integral. The DVR model lemma supplies Noetherianity, finite presentation and flatness.

source.place: Base steps 1--3; coefficient normal form and DVR algebra.

proof.text: Apply the fibre calculation over each algebraically closed residue field: the fibre is a Laurent line or two transverse axes. At the crossing apply monomial completion with $J=(xy)$ to obtain $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$. These are the required connected nodal geometric fibres.

source.place: Base step 4; geometric fibres and compatible monomial truncations.

proof.text: The DVR model lemma gives all local dimensions and the regular Laurent complement. In its regular ambient ring $P$, the displayed initial forms have order one exactly for $n=1$; the hypersurface criterion therefore gives regularity at $o$ exactly in that case. The smooth-trait-curve lemma gives the separate smooth-curve assertions.

For $n\ge2$ the blowup $B_n$ of the affine scheme $M_n$ is computed on the one-piece affine cover $\{M_n\}$: its local model is the affine blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_I\operatorname{Spec}A_n$, $I=(\pi,x,y)$ the ideal of the reduced point $o$, and the cover-independence theorem identifies the glued blowup with it over $M_n$. Specialize the chart-algebra theorem to $a=\pi$. It gives precisely the three stated charts, structure maps, overlaps and extended centre ideals. Apply the three-chart gluing theorem to this cover: the blowup is flat with connected reduced nodal geometric fibres and has exactly the stated possible middle singularity.

source.place: Base steps 8--10; divisors.tex Tag 0804 and explicit three-chart fibre gluing.

proof.text: The chart-algebra theorem identifies the exceptional scheme with the reciprocal gluing over $k$, with $\epsilon=1$ for $n=2$ and $0$ otherwise. The exceptional-curve theorem gives the smooth conic or two projective lines, including their reduced intersection, after algebraic closure. Through the identification of step 4, the affine complement theorem gives the isomorphism off $V(I)=\{o\}$.

source.place: Base steps 10--12 and complement part of 13.

proof.text: Etale maps are flat, so the chartwise flat-pullback theorem identifies each displayed chart and overlap and extends each exceptional fibre along the actual residue-field map. Apply the stalk-invariants theorem to both legs of a common pointed etale neighbourhood. Over a closed point, the etale-fibre theorem makes the chosen fibre singleton open and reduced. Choose an ambient open inducing that singleton; the pulled-back centre there is exactly the reduced chosen point. Intersect the opens for the two legs. The comparison thus identifies the blowups at those reduced points.
